paper_metadata.title: The effects of Ta additions on the phase compositions and high temperature properties of Pt base alloys

evidence.quote: In this investigation the effect of Ta on strength, phase composition, lattice misﬁt andγ′volume fraction are assessed. Starting from the composition with 12 at.% Al, 5 at.% Cr and Pt balance, precipitation hardened Pt–Al–Cr–Ta alloys were analysed.

The specimen was quenched very rapidly in liquid Ga.
In the ternary alloy Ta0 the distribution of the precipitates is monodispers throughout the sample with only one particle size distribution, with an edge length of 50–100 nm (Fig. 1 a).
The γ′ phase with a composition close to Pt3(Al, Ta, Cr) is dark shaded, while the bright phase is the Pt rich solid solution matrix.
In addition to relatively large γ′ areas, very ﬁne precipitations of 50–150 nm in size are observed.
In Fig. 2 c and d only relatively coarse γ′ particles with 1–5 /H9262m in size are observed.
The absence ofγ′peaks in the XRD diagram of Ta9 alloy can be explained with the low γ′volume fraction (14%, see Fig. 4) and the small size of the γ′particles of 50–200 nm.
At 9% Ta the distribution of precipitations is monodispers: particles of about the same size are arranged periodically and oriented. They are cuboidal and their size varies between 50 and 200 nm.
All alloys with the exception of Ta12 show two-phase structures after all annealing temperatures.
Ta additions up to 9 at.% lead to signiﬁcant enhancement of high-temperature strength, whereas at both investigated temperatures a decrease in maximum compression stress was observed for Ta12.

The alloy Ta12 has a single-phase structure. Its high-temperature strength is much lower than that of Ta9. But in comparison with the two-phase system Ta0 the maximum compression stress is still higher. In this case the solid solution strengthening by Ta provides a higher strength increase than by γ′precipitate hardening with a volume fraction of 19% but with large and irregular shaped precipitations.
Pt–Al alloys attain high creep strength by precipitation hardening of the face-centred cubic matrix phase by the L1 2 ordered intermetallic γ′ phase Pt3Al (analogous to Ni base superalloys).
